Therefore, we are herein amending the proposed rule, and conclude that as a general rule the commercial zone of a municipality which is a consolidated government includes (a) all points within the boundaries of the consolidated government, (b) all points beyond the boundaries of the consolidated government which were at any time within the commercial zone of the formerly independent core municipality, (c) when the present population of the formerly independent core municiaplity is identifiable, all points beyond the boundaries of the consolidated government which are within the territory determined by the most recent population-mileage formula measured from the limits of the formerly independent core municipality, and (d) all of any municipality wholly surrounded, or so surrounded except for a water boundary, by the consolidate government or any other municipality included under the terms of (a), (b), or (c) above. This rule is more in keeping with our general intent and should eliminate the need for municipalities which would have been adversely affected by the rule proposed in the Interim Report to petition the Commission for individual expansion.
International Boundary Municipalities - The population-mileage formula was revised so as to no longer confine commercial zones to areas in the United States, thus including in the zones of the United States municipalities on or near international borders such foreign municipalities and areas as fall within the zones under the formula. See Rio Grande Border-Comm. Zones & Term.
